18:21.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَعۡثَرۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ لِيَعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّ وَأَنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهَآ إِذۡ يَتَنَٰزَعُونَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ أَمۡرَهُمۡۖ فَقَالُواْ ٱبۡنُواْ عَلَيۡهِم بُنۡيَٰنࣰ اۖ رَّبُّهُمۡ أَعۡلَمُ بِهِمۡۚ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ غَلَبُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرِهِمۡ لَنَتَّخِذَنَّ عَلَيۡهِم مَّسۡجِدࣰ ا
18:21.en: And in like manner We disclosed them (to the people of the city) that they might know that the promise of Allah is true, and that, as for the Hour, there is no doubt concerning it. When (the people of the city) disputed of their case among themselves, they said: Build over them a building; their Lord knoweth best concerning them. Those who won their point said: We verily shall build a place of worship over them

18:28.ar: وَٱصۡبِرۡ نَفۡسَكَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَدَوٰةِ وَٱلۡعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجۡهَهُۥۖ وَلَا تَعۡدُ عَيۡنَاكَ عَنۡهُمۡ تُرِيدُ زِينَةَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَا تُطِعۡ مَنۡ أَغۡفَلۡنَا قَلۡبَهُۥ عَن ذِكۡرِنَا وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُهُۥ فُرُطࣰ ا
18:28.en: Restrain thyself along with those who cry unto their Lord at morn and evening, seeking His Countenance; and let not thine eyes overlook them, desiring the pomp of the life of the world; and obey not him whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who followeth his own lust and whose case hath been abandoned

9:18.ar: إِنَّمَا يَعۡمُرُ مَسَٰجِدَ ٱللَّهِ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَلَمۡ يَخۡشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَۖ فَعَسَىٰٓ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَن يَكُونُواْ مِنَ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
9:18.en: He only shall tend Allah's sanctuaries who believeth in Allah and the Last Day and observeth proper worship and payeth the poor-due and feareth none save Allah. For such (only) is it possible that they can be of the rightly guided

18:22.ar: سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَٰثَةࣱ رَّابِعُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ وَيَقُولُونَ خَمۡسَةࣱ سَادِسُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ رَجۡمَۢا بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ وَيَقُولُونَ سَبۡعَةࣱ وَثَامِنُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡۚ قُل رَّبِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِم مَّا يَعۡلَمُهُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱۗ فَلَا تُمَارِ فِيهِمۡ إِلَّا مِرَآءࣰ ظَٰهِرࣰ ا وَلَا تَسۡتَفۡتِ فِيهِم مِّنۡهُمۡ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:22.en: (Some) will say: They were three, their dog the fourth, and (some) say: Five, their dog the sixth, guessing at random; and (some) say: Seven, and their dog the eighth. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord is Best Aware of their number. None knoweth them save a few. So contend not concerning them except with an outward contending, and ask not any of them to pronounce concerning them

tJ24vLWK_AA.title: Activism, Our Path Forward: Companionship and Masajid
tJ24vLWK_AA.one_line: Final lessons from the People of the Cave: the masjid as the community's centre, holding on to righteous companions, and not arguing over trivia.
tJ24vLWK_AA.summary: Closing his activism series built on the People of the Cave, he notes the young men took their stand briefly yet its fruit came three hundred years later, when they woke to find their faces on the coins; we are responsible for the effort, Allah for the timing. He then gives three final points. First, the people said 'let us build a masjid over them': not a ruling on graves but a reminder that every community needs a centre. The Prophet went to the masjid first on returning from travel and carried stones to build it himself. Muslims have decentralized the masjid, taking their news from hostile media and waiting in the car rather than knowing their children's teachers, and the ummah has paid for it. Masjids need not be fancy, only full, welcoming and service-oriented, and friction among members is no reason to opt out. Second, keep yourself patiently with those who call on their Lord morning and evening; a companion who leads you to Allah is the greatest blessing after guidance, which is why the Prophet called his followers companions. Third, do not argue over how many sleepers there were; activists fail when trivia distracts them. He ends by asking each person to bring a Muslim who has drifted back to the masjid.

outline.heading: Opening
A brief stand, three hundred years of fruit
outline.gist: The youths had nothing, yet took their stand for a short time, and its result took 300 years. The Quran will be argued against us on the Day of Judgment: why did you not dedicate yourself to the cause?

outline.heading: Why they were woken: faces on the coins
outline.gist: Only Allah could keep someone asleep for 300 years. They woke, sent silver coins to buy food, and found that the currency of the land now bore their own faces.

outline.heading: Time is Allah's, effort is ours
outline.gist: The kingdom changed because of them, though it took 300 years. Time belongs to Allah; we are responsible for the activism and the effort. They thought they could do little, and Allah woke them to see otherwise.

outline.heading: Point eight: 'we will build a masjid over them'
outline.gist: Three points remain of the ten he drew from the story. Those who prevailed over the sleepers' affair resolved to build a masjid over them (18:21).

outline.heading: Every community needs a centre
outline.gist: The verse is not about graves in masjids; it is that people need a place to remember, learn and gather. Ibn Umar reports the Prophet went to the masjid and prayed two rak'ahs before going home from a journey.

outline.heading: Where they learned and heard the news
outline.gist: The masjid was where the companions were educated and mentored and learned what the ummah faced next. Today people go home to CNN or media funded by those killing our brothers and sisters.

outline.heading: We decentralized the masjid
outline.gist: We made the masjid peripheral: parents drop their children and wait in the car, never meeting the teacher or seeing what the masjid needs from them.

outline.heading: The first thing he built in Madinah
outline.gist: On arriving in Madinah the Prophet built the masjid immediately. A community cannot survive without these places, and they need not be large.

outline.heading: Full, welcoming and service-oriented
outline.gist: Masjids should be full of Muslims, welcoming and a place anyone in need comes to for support. Without a centre we do not even know who among us is struggling.

outline.heading: Carrying stones and the builders' chant
outline.gist: The Prophet carried stones himself. The companions chanted that sitting while he worked would be misguided, and he answered that there is no life but the life of the Hereafter. Uthman, unused to labour, struggled with the work.

outline.heading: Uthman and Ammar
outline.gist: Ali recited a rhyme contrasting those who build masjids with one who avoids the dust; Ammar repeated it, Uthman took it as aimed at him and threatened him, and the Prophet said Ammar was the skin between his eyes and nose.

outline.heading: Where brotherhood and friction both began
outline.gist: The masjid is where brotherhood began and also where people first rubbed each other the wrong way. Offence is human; the answer is to come back and work it out.

outline.heading: You cannot opt out
outline.gist: There is nowhere else to go: these people are your family for better or worse. Staying home has been tried, and the death toll in the Holy Land is its result.

outline.heading: Interlude
Point nine: keep yourself with those who call on their Lord
outline.gist: He recites 18:28: keep yourself patiently with those who call on their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face, and do not look past them.

outline.heading: How rare such companions are
outline.gist: If you are blessed with people who walk this path with you and do not hold on to them with all your might, you have not understood life. Do not obey those whose hearts are heedless; they may seem to have more fun.

outline.heading: He called them companions, meaning friends
outline.gist: The Prophet did not call his followers 'my followers' but 'my companions', a word meaning friends, though they walked behind him and learned from him.

outline.heading: Why the Cave, and the masjids we left
outline.gist: In Arabic: he chose the People of the Cave for this series on standing up and sacrifice because no Quranic story conveys it better and we read it weekly. Allah closes the story with the value of masjids; many came from lands full of masjids yet did not treat them as they should.

outline.heading: The masjid at the centre of the city
outline.gist: People spent, married, learned and were raised in the masjid. When that value was stripped away the ummah lost its way, and it stays lost until its people return to fill the houses of Allah (9:18).

outline.heading: A righteous companion after guidance
outline.gist: A companion who calls you to Allah, guides you by his state before his words and walks with you on the lonely road is the greatest blessing after guidance; neglecting one shows you know nothing of life. The poet's advice: bear a friend's faults or live alone.

outline.heading: Point ten: do not argue over their number
outline.gist: An activist falls when distracted by details that do not matter. People will say three, five or seven sleepers; do not dispute it (18:22). Whatever our differences, we are people of one qiblah, one God and one Messenger.

outline.heading: Bring a Muslim back to the masjid
outline.gist: Outreach does not have to mean converts: look for Muslims who have drifted and bring them back to the house of Allah, which is itself the outreach, so they find there what you found. The youths of the cave took a stand to bring people back to Allah.

outline.heading: Interlude
One family of many nations
outline.gist: With 25 or 26 nationalities in the room, diversity is a beauty if the community functions as one family with each other's back. The youth must take up activism now rather than waste another generation; change will come, even if, as with the cave, after we are gone.

outline.heading: Outro

28:53.ar: وَإِذَا يُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡ قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ مُسۡلِمِينَ
28:53.en: And when it is recited unto them, they say: We believe in it. Lo! it is the Truth from our Lord. Lo! even before it we were of those who surrender (unto Him)

28:54.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُؤۡتَوۡنَ أَجۡرَهُم مَّرَّتَيۡنِ بِمَا صَبَرُواْ وَيَدۡرَءُونَ بِٱلۡحَسَنَةِ ٱلسَّيِّئَةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
28:54.en: These will be given their reward twice over, because they are steadfast and repel evil with good, and spend of that wherewith We have provided them

28:55.ar: وَإِذَا سَمِعُواْ ٱللَّغۡوَ أَعۡرَضُواْ عَنۡهُ وَقَالُواْ لَنَآ أَعۡمَٰلُنَا وَلَكُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلُكُمۡ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡ لَا نَبۡتَغِي ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
28:55.en: And when they hear vanity they withdraw from it and say: Unto us our works and unto you your works. Peace be unto you! We desire not the ignorant

28:56.ar: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهۡدِي مَنۡ أَحۡبَبۡتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
28:56.en: Lo! thou (O Muhammad) guidest not whom thou lovest, but Allah guideth whom He will. And He is Best Aware of those who walk aright

5:73.ar: لَّقَدۡ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ثَالِثُ ثَلَٰثَةࣲۘ وَمَا مِنۡ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّآ إِلَٰهࣱ وَٰحِدࣱۚ وَإِن لَّمۡ يَنتَهُواْ عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
5:73.en: They surely disbelieve who say: Lo! Allah is the third of three; when there is no Allah save the One Allah. If they desist not from so saying a painful doom will fall on those of them who disbelieve

41:34.ar: وَلَا تَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ وَلَا ٱلسَّيِّئَةُۚ ٱدۡفَعۡ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَكَ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ عَدَٰوَةࣱ كَأَنَّهُۥ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمࣱ‏
41:34.en: The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend

41:35.ar: وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
41:35.en: But none is granted it save those who are steadfast, and none is granted it save the owner of great happiness

2:124.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱبۡتَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَٰتࣲ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّۖ قَالَ إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامࣰ اۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِيۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهۡدِي ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:124.en: And (remember) when his Lord tried Abraham with (His) commands, and he fulfilled them, He said: Lo! I have appointed thee a leader for mankind. (Abraham) said: And of my offspring (will there be leaders)? He said: My covenant includeth not wrong-doers

37:113.ar: وَبَٰرَكۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسۡحَٰقَۚ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحۡسِنࣱ وَظَالِمࣱ لِّنَفۡسِهِۦ مُبِينࣱ‏
37:113.en: And We blessed him and Isaac. And of their seed are some who do good, and some who plainly wrong themselves

7:199.ar: خُذِ ٱلۡعَفۡوَ وَأۡمُرۡ بِٱلۡعُرۡفِ وَأَعۡرِضۡ عَنِ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
7:199.en: Keep to forgiveness (O Muhammad), and enjoin kindness, and turn away from the ignorant

7:200.ar: وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ نَزۡغࣱ فَٱسۡتَعِذۡ بِٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّهُۥ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
7:200.en: And if a slander from the devil wound thee, then seek refuge in Allah. Lo! He is Hearer, Knower

43:31.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡلَا نُزِّلَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَتَيۡنِ عَظِيمٍ
43:31.en: And they say: If only this Qur'an had been revealed to some great man of the two towns

11:42.ar: وَهِيَ تَجۡرِي بِهِمۡ فِي مَوۡجࣲ كَٱلۡجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبۡنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِي مَعۡزِلࣲ يَٰبُنَيَّ ٱرۡكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
11:42.en: And it sailed with them amid waves like mountains, and Noah cried unto his son - and he was standing aloof - O my son! Come ride with us, and be not with the disbelievers

11:43.ar: قَالَ سَـَٔاوِيٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلࣲ يَعۡصِمُنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِۚ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَۚ وَحَالَ بَيۡنَهُمَا ٱلۡمَوۡجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُغۡرَقِينَ
11:43.en: He said: I shall betake me to some mountain that will save me from the water. (Noah) said: This day there is none that saveth from the commandment of Allah save him on whom He hath had mercy. And the wave came in between them, so he was among the drowned

6:74.ar: ۞وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ ءَازَرَ أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصۡنَامًا ءَالِهَةً إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰكَ وَقَوۡمَكَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
6:74.en: (Remember) when Abraham said unto his father Azar: Takest thou idols for gods? Lo! I see thee and thy folk in error manifest

G4b5W8A5KS0.title: Arabic Tafsir of Surat al-Qasas: Repelling Evil with Good and 'You Cannot Guide Whom You Love', Verses 53-56
G4b5W8A5KS0.one_line: Believing People of the Book: patience, repelling evil with good, turning from idle talk; and why no one, not even the Prophet, can guide whom he loves.
G4b5W8A5KS0.summary: The sheikh opens by balancing two errors: diluting the clear warnings of the Quran, and acting as judges of people's final fates, which only revelation can tell. Verses 53-55 praise People of the Book who believed: they get a double reward for their patience, repel evil with good, spend, and turn away from idle talk. Repelling evil with good follows from the surah's lesson that you do not know why someone harmed you, and returning harm risks exceeding it. He cites the words on the Prophet's sword and the story of the man who drew the Prophet's own sword on him and was forgiven. The ummah's goodness is not by birth but by following the Prophet, as Ibrahim was told about his offspring. On idle talk he warns against being dragged into the mud, against social media where young men attack al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar, and against speaking ill of any scholar, even those who sided with the regime in Syria; reject the stance, not the person. WhatsApp forwards are mostly fabricated. Verse 56, revealed about Abu Talib, teaches that guidance belongs to Allah alone: his own predictions about children have always been wrong, and our role is only to point the way and guard our own guidance.

outline.heading: Warn of the fire without assigning anyone's fate
outline.gist: We state clearly that shirk leads to the fire and hold ourselves to it, but neither dilute the deen nor claim to know where any individual will end up.

outline.heading: Only revelation tells us who is in paradise or hell
outline.gist: You were not inside anyone's heart or present at his end; we know fates only when Allah or the Prophet told us.

outline.heading: Believing People of the Book receive a double reward
outline.gist: Some of the best companions and early scholars were former Jews and Christians; the Quran openly praises them here.

outline.heading: Repelling evil with good
outline.gist: Dar' means defending yourself with something; whoever understands al-Qasas assumes the offender may have a reason, and retaliating risks exceeding the harm.

outline.heading: Try it once and see the fruit
outline.gist: Answering harm with kindness shames almost everyone into changing.

outline.heading: The words on the Prophet's sword
outline.gist: Give to whoever denies you, pardon whoever wrongs you, do good to whoever harms you; he never got angry for himself, only when someone else was wronged.

outline.heading: The man who drew the Prophet's own sword
outline.gist: While the army rested, a man took his sword and asked who would protect him; the Prophet said 'Allah', the sword fell, and he pardoned the man.

outline.heading: Goodness is found in all people
outline.gist: Patience, repelling evil and spending: Allah sees good beyond this ummah, whose own goodness rises and falls with how well it follows the Prophet.

outline.heading: Not by birth or lineage
outline.gist: Ibrahim asked for leadership for his offspring and was told it does not reach wrongdoers; whoever is slowed by his deeds is not hastened by his lineage.

outline.heading: Turning away from idle talk
outline.gist: Laghw is worthless speech; one with a mission has no time for it, and the Quran says turn from the ignorant and seek refuge when provoked.

outline.heading: Do not descend into the sewer
outline.gist: Whoever excels at petty quarrels wants to drag you down; 'to us our deeds and to you yours, peace be upon you'.

outline.heading: 'We seek not the ignorant' and the internet
outline.gist: Most of what is online, especially for those who met social media after forty, is worthless and lowers your intellect.

outline.heading: Everyone now speaks about the deen
outline.gist: Once one earned the right to speak through years of learning; now a 25-year-old attacks the creed of al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar.

outline.heading: Never speak ill of a scholar
outline.gist: Even scholars who stood with the dictator in Syria will answer to Allah; reject the stance and debate views with evidence, but do not tear down the person.

outline.heading: Learn from scholars you know, not random voices
outline.gist: Listening to people whose background and circumstances you do not know, then applying their words to your family, breeds discord.

outline.heading: WhatsApp forwards are mostly fabricated
outline.gist: Sayings attributed to Ali, moral tales and the 'nightingale' poem supposedly recited to Harun al-Rashid are invented.

outline.heading: Answer idle talk with peace and walk away
outline.gist: You win hearts this way and Allah may guide them later; unguided religious content online is more dangerous than cartoons or football.

outline.heading: 'You cannot guide whom you love': Abu Talib
outline.gist: The verse is linked to Abu Talib; the stronger view is that he did not accept Islam, though some Sunni scholars refrain from asserting it, and the Prophet at least did not hear what would reassure him.

outline.heading: The Prophet's grief and Allah's choice
outline.gist: Unlike Khadijah, whose place in paradise he knew, his uncle's fate grieved him; Allah guides according to what He knows lies in hearts.

outline.heading: Guidance is not given by our wishes
outline.gist: Someone you dislike may be guided and someone you hoped for may stray; the Jews and the chiefs of Quraysh wished the message had come to their own.

outline.heading: Predictions about children always prove wrong
outline.gist: Every time he read good or bad in a child he was mistaken; Nuh's son strayed and Ibrahim's father was an idolater.

outline.heading: Our role is to point the way, not to guide
outline.gist: If the Prophet could not guide whom he loved, we cannot; we give information, and Allah turns it into guidance in one listener and not another.

outline.heading: Guard your own guidance
outline.gist: The surah's lesson turns you to your own story: ask to be used as a means of guidance, as in 'that Allah guides one man through you', and hold on to your own.

65:2.ar: فَإِذَا بَلَغۡنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمۡسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفٍ أَوۡ فَارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفࣲ وَأَشۡهِدُواْ ذَوَيۡ عَدۡلࣲ مِّنكُمۡ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلشَّهَٰدَةَ لِلَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ يُوعَظُ بِهِۦ مَن كَانَ يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ مَخۡرَجࣰ ا
65:2.en: Then, when they have reached their term, take them back in kindness or part from them in kindness, and call to witness two just men among you, and keep your testimony upright for Allah. Whoso believeth in Allah and the Last Day is exhorted to act thus. And whosoever keepeth his duty to Allah, Allah will appoint a way out for him

65:3.ar: وَيَرۡزُقۡهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا يَحۡتَسِبُۚ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسۡبُهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَٰلِغُ أَمۡرِهِۦۚ قَدۡ جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدۡرࣰ ا
65:3.en: And will provide for him from (a quarter) whence he hath no expectation. And whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him. Lo! Allah bringeth His command to pass. Allah hath set a measure for all things

65:4.ar: وَٱلَّٰٓـِٔي يَئِسۡنَ مِنَ ٱلۡمَحِيضِ مِن نِّسَآئِكُمۡ إِنِ ٱرۡتَبۡتُمۡ فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلَٰثَةُ أَشۡهُرࣲ وَٱلَّٰٓـِٔي لَمۡ يَحِضۡنَۚ وَأُوْلَٰتُ ٱلۡأَحۡمَالِ أَجَلُهُنَّ أَن يَضَعۡنَ حَمۡلَهُنَّۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِۦ يُسۡرࣰ ا
65:4.en: And for such of your women as despair of menstruation, if ye doubt, their period (of waiting) shall be three months, along with those who have it not. And for those with child, their period shall be till they bring forth their burden. And whosoever keepeth his duty to Allah, He maketh his course easy for him

65:5.ar: ذَٰلِكَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ أَنزَلَهُۥٓ إِلَيۡكُمۡۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ يُكَفِّرۡ عَنۡهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِۦ وَيُعۡظِمۡ لَهُۥٓ أَجۡرًا
65:5.en: That is the commandment of Allah which He revealeth unto you. And whoso keepeth his duty to Allah, He will remit from him his evil deeds and magnify reward for him

65:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِذَا طَلَّقۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ وَأَحۡصُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّكُمۡۖ لَا تُخۡرِجُوهُنَّ مِنۢ بُيُوتِهِنَّ وَلَا يَخۡرُجۡنَ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةࣲ مُّبَيِّنَةࣲۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ ظَلَمَ نَفۡسَهُۥۚ لَا تَدۡرِي لَعَلَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحۡدِثُ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ أَمۡرࣰ ا
65:1.en: O Prophet! When ye (men) put away women, put them away for their (legal) period and reckon the period, and keep your duty to Allah, your Lord. Expel them not from their houses nor let them go forth unless they commit open immorality. Such are the limits (imposed by) Allah; and whoso transgresseth Allah's limits, he verily wrongeth his soul. Thou knowest not: it may be that Allah will afterward bring some new thing to pass

33:37.ar: وَإِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيٓ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡسِكۡ عَلَيۡكَ زَوۡجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخۡفِي فِي نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ وَتَخۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخۡشَىٰهُۖ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدࣱ مِّنۡهَا وَطَرࣰ ا زَوَّجۡنَٰكَهَا لِكَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجࣱ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِ أَدۡعِيَآئِهِمۡ إِذَا قَضَوۡاْ مِنۡهُنَّ وَطَرࣰ اۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا
33:37.en: And when thou saidst unto him on whom Allah hath conferred favour and thou hast conferred favour: Keep thy wife to thyself, and fear Allah. And thou didst hide in thy mind that which Allah was to bring to light, and thou didst fear mankind whereas Allah hath a better right that thou shouldst fear Him. So when Zeyd had performed that necessary formality (of divorce) from her, We gave her unto thee in marriage, so that (henceforth) there may be no sin for believers in respect of wives of their adopted sons, when the latter have performed the necessary formality (of release) from them. The commandment of Allah must be fulfilled

5:89.ar: لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغۡوِ فِيٓ أَيۡمَٰنِكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ ٱلۡأَيۡمَٰنَۖ فَكَفَّٰرَتُهُۥٓ إِطۡعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَٰكِينَ مِنۡ أَوۡسَطِ مَا تُطۡعِمُونَ أَهۡلِيكُمۡ أَوۡ كِسۡوَتُهُمۡ أَوۡ تَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةࣲۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامࣲۚ ذَٰلِكَ كَفَّٰرَةُ أَيۡمَٰنِكُمۡ إِذَا حَلَفۡتُمۡۚ وَٱحۡفَظُوٓاْ أَيۡمَٰنَكُمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
5:89.en: Allah will not take you to task for that which is unintentional in your oaths, but He will take you to task for the oaths which ye swear in earnest. The expiation thereof is the feeding of ten of the needy with the average of that wherewith ye feed your own folk, or the clothing of them, or the liberation of a slave, and for him who findeth not (the wherewithal to do so) then a three days' fast. This is the expiation of your oaths when ye have sworn; and keep your oaths. Thus Allah expoundeth unto you His revelations in order that ye may give thanks

2:228.ar: وَٱلۡمُطَلَّقَٰتُ يَتَرَبَّصۡنَ بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ ثَلَٰثَةَ قُرُوٓءࣲۚ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَن يَكۡتُمۡنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِيٓ أَرۡحَامِهِنَّ إِن كُنَّ يُؤۡمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ إِنۡ أَرَادُوٓاْ إِصۡلَٰحࣰ اۚ وَلَهُنَّ مِثۡلُ ٱلَّذِي عَلَيۡهِنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيۡهِنَّ دَرَجَةࣱۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
2:228.en: Women who are divorced shall wait, keeping themselves apart, three (monthly) courses. And it is not lawful for them that they should conceal that which Allah hath created in their wombs if they are believers in Allah and the Last Day. And their husbands would do better to take them back in that case if they desire a reconciliation. And they (women) have rights similar to those (of men) over them in kindness, and men are a degree above them. Allah is Mighty, Wise

MlPAHrLX1iE.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Talaq, Part 2 (65:2-5)
MlPAHrLX1iE.one_line: Marriage defaults and fairness, his view that divorce requires two witnesses, the waiting periods, and the surah's fourfold call to taqwa and tawakkul.
MlPAHrLX1iE.summary: He begins with why Muslim families are weakening: marriage has slipped past its sweet spot in the early to mid twenties, and spouses enter without knowing their obligations. He lays out the default Islamic arrangement: the man provides and always protects, the woman maintains the household, she keeps her own earnings, and any departure from the default must be rebalanced fairly, because love survives only where each spouse feels the other is carrying their weight; most divorces he sees come from one partner carrying far more. On verse 2 he argues, against the dominant view of the four schools but with minority opinions and many contemporary Syrian scholars and courts, that two witnesses are obligatory for divorce as for marriage, so a divorce blurted in anger without witnesses counts as a broken oath requiring expiation and repentance. He then treats the famous promises: whoever has taqwa is given a way out and unexpected provision, and whoever relies on Allah finds Him sufficient. He defines taqwa as avoiding what will harm you in this life or the next and applies it to refusing poisonous words during divorce, which wound children most. He explains the waiting periods for postmenopausal, non-menstruating and pregnant women, and stresses that good conduct is commanded by Allah, not owed only if the other spouse reciprocates. The page repeats taqwa four times with distinct promises.

outline.heading: Understand the Quran through its first audience
outline.gist: To grasp the surah one must understand how the companions viewed divorce when it was revealed.

outline.heading: A balanced approach as the Muslim family weakens
outline.gist: Faiths have long disputed divorce; Islam permits it when necessary within rulings and ethics, at a time when Muslim families are less solid than before.

outline.heading: Muslim families once had far less domestic abuse
outline.gist: Without alcohol and gambling, leading drivers of abuse and debt, Muslim homes were historically more stable.

outline.heading: Maturity, not age, makes early marriage work
outline.gist: Very young and very late marriages both fare poorly; the issue is maturity rather than a number.

outline.heading: His grandparents and blaming the previous generation
outline.gist: His grandfather married at 13 because he was already working; children only go as far as their parents' generation lets them.

outline.heading: The sweet spot for men: marry while still building
outline.gist: A man should marry when mature but not yet established, so he needs and appreciates his wife through his difficult years.

outline.heading: The sweet spot for women: the comfortable childbearing years
outline.gist: Childbearing is easiest biologically and psychologically before thirty, with rising risks after.

outline.heading: We have left the window
outline.gist: Capable men in their thirties and women in their late twenties remain unmarried; the surah also teaches the obligations of marriage.

outline.heading: Knowing your obligations before marrying
outline.gist: Understanding what marriage requires leads people to marry at the right time with the right expectations.

outline.heading: The default: he provides, she maintains the household
outline.gist: By default the man is fully responsible for finances and the woman for the safety and running of the home, though this can change.

outline.heading: Protection is the default that never changes
outline.gist: The man is always the protector; if the ship sinks she takes the raft.

outline.heading: Change the default, rebalance the load
outline.gist: If she contributes half the income he must do half the household work; otherwise she carries most of the load and stops valuing him.

outline.heading: Her entitlement from his income
outline.gist: Beyond food, clothing and shelter, a wife is entitled to a share of his income as her own, as far as he can afford.

outline.heading: Her money is hers; be clear about joint accounts
outline.gist: A wife's earnings belong to her; pooled money must be matched by a proportional share of responsibilities.

outline.heading: The reverse imbalance and its fallout
outline.gist: A man earning everything and also doing half the housework grows disgruntled; people sense injustice quickly.

outline.heading: Advice to husbands: never take her money
outline.gist: Men feel entitled after doing chores and women resent spending their earnings on husbands, so the husband should provide and leave her income to her.

outline.heading: Either spouse can revert to the default
outline.gist: Couples like two physicians may agree on different arrangements, but either can return to the default at any time.

outline.heading: The pattern behind the divorces he sees
outline.gist: Usually one spouse has carried 65 to 70 percent of the load and is exhausted while the other cannot understand why.

outline.heading: Love exists only where there is fairness
outline.gist: Love grows when each feels the other does more than expected; gratitude between spouses, like an older couple who value each other, keeps marriage strong.

outline.heading: Most divorces are avoidable: Zayd and Zaynab
outline.gist: Some couples are simply incompatible, like Zayd and Zaynab, but about 90 percent of divorces stem from misunderstood obligations.

outline.heading: Defaults can be changed if the result is fair
outline.gist: These are the scholars' long-standing positions; contracts can stipulate otherwise as long as everyone carries their weight.

outline.heading: Reconcile once unfairness is fixed
outline.gist: The waiting period lets someone examine the marriage and correct imbalances so the couple can hold on with ma'ruf, or part respectfully.

outline.heading: Two just witnesses
outline.gist: The witnesses must be people of religious responsibility, knowledge and impeccable character.

outline.heading: Witnesses for reconciliation only, or for divorce too?
outline.gist: The prevailing view applies the witnesses to taking her back and as recommended; opinions within the Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali schools extend it to divorce.

outline.heading: No evidence to make the command a mere recommendation
outline.gist: A Quranic command needs supporting evidence to be downgraded, and none exists; restricting it to reconciliation reflected the norms of the time.

outline.heading: Enter with witnesses, leave with witnesses
outline.gist: Many Syrian scholars made witnesses obligatory for divorce in court; a marriage should not end on a whim when it began by contract.

outline.heading: When men no longer keep their word
outline.gist: Verbal divorce suited people who would die for their word; once integrity declined, a documented exit became necessary.

outline.heading: What the four schools agree on
outline.gist: Repeating the word in one period still counts as one divorce, and divorce at a forbidden time takes effect but is sinful.

outline.heading: His view: without witnesses, a broken oath
outline.gist: An unwitnessed pronouncement is treated like a broken oath requiring expiation, while a real divorce needs two witnesses.

outline.heading: The angry husband who regrets in fifteen minutes
outline.gist: He no longer takes these daily calls; a man who divorces in a temper should pay expiation, repent and arguably lose control of divorce.

outline.heading: How Muslim family courts handle it today
outline.gist: Many courts follow this view because of declining integrity and absurd conditional divorces; marriage is not a game.

outline.heading: Establish testimony for Allah
outline.gist: Witnesses must truly witness and speak truthfully later, which shows the weight Allah gives to testimony here.

outline.heading: Wa'z: a gentle reminder for believers
outline.gist: Wa'z is an emotionally uplifting reminder; Allah kindly urges those who believe in Him and the Last Day to keep these rulings.

outline.heading: Taqwa brings a way out and unexpected provision
outline.gist: Two promises: an exit from every difficulty and provision from routes one never anticipated, the second mention of taqwa in the surah.

outline.heading: Whoever relies on Allah, He suffices
outline.gist: With true reliance one needs no one else besides Allah.

outline.heading: The two great tools, placed where they are most needed
outline.gist: Taqwa and tawakkul keep a person from losing their faith and ethics when dealing with a spouse at the point of breakup.

outline.heading: Allah accomplishes His decree; everything has its measure
outline.gist: What is written will happen, so do not waste life resenting it; divorce is meant to end misery, not break people.

outline.heading: Timeless verses, placed here on purpose
outline.gist: These verses apply to everyone, but they sit here because divorce is when people most need to be at their best.

outline.heading: Taqwa as one simple question
outline.gist: Will this decision harm me in this life or the next? If yes, do not do it.

outline.heading: The spectrum: avoid the harmful tenth
outline.gist: Most choices are permissible; taqwa only excludes the harmful portion, while asking whether each act pleases Allah is the path of the especially godly.

outline.heading: Holding back the poisonous word
outline.gist: Taqwa in divorce means refusing to say the one wounding thing only you know, said purely out of spite.

outline.heading: Tawakkul: do not stay out of fear of the future
outline.gist: Do your best and leave outcomes to Allah rather than remaining in a marriage out of fear.

outline.heading: Harsh words wound the children, not the spouse
outline.gist: The spouses have already hurt each other; insults now harm the children and families, and a child must never be told such things about a parent.

outline.heading: Spiritual relief within a legal surah
outline.gist: Taqwa and tawakkul appear together here, giving spirit to a surah otherwise full of juristic detail.

outline.heading: Interlude
Repeated reminders of taqwa between rulings
outline.gist: Amid technical rulings Allah keeps returning to taqwa so people behave well during divorce, releasing with excellence.

outline.heading: Women who have despaired of menstruation
outline.gist: The verse turns to divorced women past menopause; the word carries both despair and no longer expecting.

outline.heading: Three months for doubt or for those who never menstruated
outline.gist: Menstruating women wait three cycles; those unsure after menopause and those who never menstruate wait three months.

outline.heading: The pregnant woman's term ends with delivery
outline.gist: Her waiting period ends when the pregnancy ends, whether by birth or miscarriage, even days after the divorce.

outline.heading: The waiting periods summarized
outline.gist: Three cycles, three months, or until the end of pregnancy, with school differences on how cycles are counted.

outline.heading: Taqwa brings ease; divorce is painful for both
outline.gist: The third mention promises ease, because divorce always hurts both spouses, however short or toxic the marriage.

outline.heading: The rulings exist to make it honourable
outline.gist: Right timing, staying in the home, witnesses and set periods make divorce a decision rather than an outburst.

outline.heading: Not reciprocal: the command Allah sent down
outline.gist: Good conduct is owed because Allah commanded it, not because the other spouse behaves; a spouse without taqwa confirms the separation was right.

outline.heading: Taqwa removes sins and magnifies reward
outline.gist: The fourth mention promises sins covered and reward enlarged.

outline.heading: The page with the most taqwa in the Quran
outline.gist: Four direct mentions on one page, with distinct promises of a way out, provision, ease, forgiveness and greater reward, unmatched elsewhere.

outline.heading: Outro

vNPrQmEvB5A.title: Outreach, The Way of Our Prophets: Verbal and Practical
vNPrQmEvB5A.one_line: Launching outreach month: unity around Palestine, the Prophet building from nothing, and a charge to bring one person to the masjid through practical dawah.
vNPrQmEvB5A.summary: He opens by admitting the ten months since the war began have been the hardest for Muslims in the West since 9/11, and that every topic he chooses is poured into the same pot: a weak ummah lacking unity, commitment and activism. Muslims need not agree on everything to work together, but they must agree that Palestine is central, not because its blood is worth more than Syria's, his own country's, but because it is the Holy Land and unites the ummah. Anyone devoted to the cause deserves respect whatever their ideology. History moves in cycles of sleep and awakening, and the Prophet lived in a darker time than ours, building the ummah one person at a time, so there is more hope today. He then launches August as outreach month and requires everyone to bring at least one person to the masjid, starting with Muslims at arm's length. You keep your own faith by helping others, and guidance grows as you give it. Verbal dawah is a small part; practical dawah through ethics and lifestyle does more. His own teenage story of being mocked on the way to the masjid shows that patience wins people, and that mocking those who return would kill repentance.

outline.heading: Opening
The hardest ten months since 9/11
outline.gist: Watching the bloodshed in the Holy Land while the world stays silent has made it hard to justify speaking about anything else, and hard to know whether his series have helped.

outline.heading: Every topic pours into the same pot
outline.gist: Suffering watched silently becomes trauma. Whatever he speaks about is meant to fill one pot: an ummah weakened by disunity and a lack of commitment, devotion and activism.

outline.heading: Working with those you disagree with
outline.gist: Muslims have had sects for about 1,200 of their 1,400 years; you collaborate daily at work and as a citizen with people who agree with you on almost nothing, so identify what Muslims do not disagree on.

outline.heading: Why Palestine is central
outline.gist: Not because Palestinian blood is worth more than Sudanese, Iraqi or Syrian blood, but because it is the Holy Land with al-Aqsa and it unites the ummah. Syria, his own country, lost half a million people, yet its cause does not unite Muslims the way this one does.

outline.heading: Respect for anyone devoted to the cause
outline.gist: Muslims have not always had a uniting cause; overlook differences, and hold in high regard anyone who gives time, wealth or life for it whatever their ideology, without disrespectful labels.

outline.heading: Leaders and minbars now arguing against it
outline.gist: He grew up when even sellouts agreed the cause must be fixed; now preachers and Muslim political leaders publicly deny its centrality, which he finds nauseating. Leaders who still carry it deserve acknowledgement.

outline.heading: A sacred cause: 150 years then, 75 years now
outline.gist: The Holy Land has always been sacred; the generation that raised Salahuddin focused on it for about 150 years until it was regained. After 75 years it must stay central, while every other cause still deserves support.

outline.heading: Always with the oppressed
outline.gist: He has listened sincerely to every opposing argument and still cannot imagine standing against the oppressed; when the oppressed include a holy land and a sacred masjid the sanctity is higher still.

outline.heading: Everything aims at the ummah's awakening
outline.gist: Whether he speaks about sleep habits, prayer, activism or outreach, every topic is directed at justice, unity and strength: the ummah's modern awakening.

outline.heading: History moves in cycles
outline.gist: Muslim history, like human history, is cyclical: awakening, justice, distraction by wealth, decline, four or five times over; awakenings require a generation that knows where it stands historically.

outline.heading: The Prophet lived in a darker time
outline.gist: He never saw the peak; Islam was established about fifteen years after his death, in the time of the caliphs. Being Muslim when it is not easy or popular makes us more like him than those who lived at the top.

outline.heading: Built one person at a time
outline.gist: He built the ummah brick by brick with Khadijah, Abu Bakr, Ali and Zayd, with perhaps sixty people after four or five years; with two billion Muslims today, despite dictators and no political unity, there is more hope.

outline.heading: Something has to click inside
outline.gist: No ingredient is missing except what is in the hearts; wait with patience, and if it does not click in this generation, work on the next, until enough Muslims live directed toward Allah.

outline.heading: A month devoted to outreach
outline.gist: It took him 23 years and may take us 100 or 150; this month is centred on dawah so that people gain tools to keep doing it all year.

outline.heading: Bring one person to the masjid
outline.gist: He requires everyone to bring at least one person to a masjid this month, starting with Muslims at arm's length who never felt comfortable there, and to make sure they find something meaningful.

outline.heading: You cannot guide whom you love
outline.gist: Everyone has friends and family who do not come; if one does not respond, move on (28:56). Guidance is a gift most people lack, so the guided are obliged to bring it close, starting with those who are only a little lost.

outline.heading: You take care of yourself by taking care of others
outline.gist: You stay committed by offering guidance to others; it is the opposite of wealth, growing the more you give it. Spreading it is the legacy of the prophets.

outline.heading: Who carries the prophets' task now
outline.gist: Allah always sent another prophet when one died; after the last, no one received a memo because the task belongs to every Muslim. The imam keeps things running inside, you bring people in from outside.

outline.heading: Verbal and practical dawah
outline.gist: Who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and acts righteously (41:33): verbal dawah is maybe 2 percent; ethics, choices and a minimalist, devoted life call people back far more.

outline.heading: Interlude
No salvation without saving the lost
outline.gist: The ummah will not succeed if its people do not feel that saving distracted brothers and sisters is part of saving the ummah, or if they write off all but the committed.

outline.heading: The Prophet's nation is all of humanity
outline.gist: A prophet's nation is everyone he was sent to teach; Muhammad's nation is all humanity, those who responded and those who did not.

outline.heading: Be willing to be vulnerable
outline.gist: Those granted the gift of response must spread it, starting at arm's length, even if it means being called a fanatic or admitting how they used to be.

outline.heading: Mocked on the way to the masjid
outline.gist: As a young teen turning to religion he was mocked daily by young men on a tractor; his sheikh told him to say nothing, since Allah tests whether you are serious. Five years later they came to learn at the masjid.

outline.heading: A good Muslim is not quiet
outline.gist: A good Muslim keeps nudging people along even when mocked; repentance is leaving the wrong path for the right one, and if every returner were mocked no one would repent.

outline.heading: You call others to keep yourself guided
outline.gist: Calling to Allah is for your own sake: you ask Him not to let you go astray, knowing your faults. Everyone is equally lost; stay committed by surrounding yourself with those who call to Allah.

outline.heading: Outro

65:6.ar: أَسۡكِنُوهُنَّ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ سَكَنتُم مِّن وُجۡدِكُمۡ وَلَا تُضَآرُّوهُنَّ لِتُضَيِّقُواْ عَلَيۡهِنَّۚ وَإِن كُنَّ أُوْلَٰتِ حَمۡلࣲ فَأَنفِقُواْ عَلَيۡهِنَّ حَتَّىٰ يَضَعۡنَ حَمۡلَهُنَّۚ فَإِنۡ أَرۡضَعۡنَ لَكُمۡ فَـَٔاتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ وَأۡتَمِرُواْ بَيۡنَكُم بِمَعۡرُوفࣲۖ وَإِن تَعَاسَرۡتُمۡ فَسَتُرۡضِعُ لَهُۥٓ أُخۡرَىٰ
65:6.en: Lodge them where ye dwell, according to your wealth, and harass them not so as to straiten life for them. And if they are with child, then spend for them till they bring forth their burden. Then, if they give suck for you, give them their due payment and consult together in kindness; but if ye make difficulties for one another, then let some other woman give suck for him (the father of the child)

65:7.ar: لِيُنفِقۡ ذُو سَعَةࣲ مِّن سَعَتِهِۦۖ وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقُهُۥ فَلۡيُنفِقۡ مِمَّآ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُۚ لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا مَآ ءَاتَىٰهَاۚ سَيَجۡعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡدَ عُسۡرࣲ يُسۡرࣰ ا
65:7.en: Let him who hath abundance spend of his abundance, and he whose provision is measured, let him spend of that which Allah hath given him. Allah asketh naught of any soul save that which He hath given it. Allah will vouchsafe, after hardship, ease

65:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِذَا طَلَّقۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ وَأَحۡصُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّكُمۡۖ لَا تُخۡرِجُوهُنَّ مِنۢ بُيُوتِهِنَّ وَلَا يَخۡرُجۡنَ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةࣲ مُّبَيِّنَةࣲۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ ظَلَمَ نَفۡسَهُۥۚ لَا تَدۡرِي لَعَلَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحۡدِثُ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ أَمۡرࣰ ا
65:1.en: O Prophet! When ye (men) put away women, put them away for their (legal) period and reckon the period, and keep your duty to Allah, your Lord. Expel them not from their houses nor let them go forth unless they commit open immorality. Such are the limits (imposed by) Allah; and whoso transgresseth Allah's limits, he verily wrongeth his soul. Thou knowest not: it may be that Allah will afterward bring some new thing to pass

65:2.ar: فَإِذَا بَلَغۡنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمۡسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفٍ أَوۡ فَارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفࣲ وَأَشۡهِدُواْ ذَوَيۡ عَدۡلࣲ مِّنكُمۡ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلشَّهَٰدَةَ لِلَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ يُوعَظُ بِهِۦ مَن كَانَ يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ مَخۡرَجࣰ ا
65:2.en: Then, when they have reached their term, take them back in kindness or part from them in kindness, and call to witness two just men among you, and keep your testimony upright for Allah. Whoso believeth in Allah and the Last Day is exhorted to act thus. And whosoever keepeth his duty to Allah, Allah will appoint a way out for him

65:4.ar: وَٱلَّٰٓـِٔي يَئِسۡنَ مِنَ ٱلۡمَحِيضِ مِن نِّسَآئِكُمۡ إِنِ ٱرۡتَبۡتُمۡ فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلَٰثَةُ أَشۡهُرࣲ وَٱلَّٰٓـِٔي لَمۡ يَحِضۡنَۚ وَأُوْلَٰتُ ٱلۡأَحۡمَالِ أَجَلُهُنَّ أَن يَضَعۡنَ حَمۡلَهُنَّۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِۦ يُسۡرࣰ ا

9OooDg4aNNo.one_line: A husband's duty of protection without control, separate finances, housing and maintenance during the waiting period, and giving according to what Allah has given.
9OooDg4aNNo.summary: He starts by separating abuse from marriage: abuse is a crime that historic Muslim courts punished with prison. He then explains the husband's permanent role as protector, which gives him a say only over genuine safety hazards, not control of his wife's movements; what counts as a hazard depends on local norms and should be agreed before marriage, since the Prophet looked forward to a time when a woman could travel alone safely. Revisiting the default division of roles, he advises working wives to keep their own money in separate accounts and recognizes household work as equal to earning, so that spouses stay grateful. After recapping the surah's rulings, he explains verse 6: during the waiting period the divorced wife must be housed at the husband's standard and not squeezed financially, maintained until birth if pregnant, and paid for breastfeeding, with terms set by what is customarily fair. From verse 7 he draws that each gives according to his means; through the meaning of qudira and the story of Yunus he shows it means restricted, not unable. He widens this into speaking only from real knowledge, playing the hand one is dealt and not trying to impress, and the need for financial compatibility. He ends with the wife's personal maintenance, which should be calculated at divorce if never paid.

outline.heading: Protection is not control
outline.gist: Rulings meant for protection become tools for limiting women's lives when misused.

outline.heading: What needs his input: reasonable safety hazards
outline.gist: A wife should raise matters that pose a reasonable safety risk; daily details should be agreed before marriage, and otherwise local norms decide.

outline.heading: Examples: neighbourhoods, the 401 and travel abroad
outline.gist: Where a woman alone is unsafe, as in places he lived, or on long highway drives or travel to a war zone, the husband may require protection or a mahram.

outline.heading: Disputes go back to the norm
outline.gist: The husband does not control her movements; disagreements are settled by what functional couples consider reasonable, as imams, counsellors or lawyers know.

outline.heading: From one protector to another, not one dictator to another
outline.gist: Marriage moves a woman from her father's protection to her husband's, not into dictatorship; everyone needs protection.

outline.heading: Protection is subjective, so discuss it first
outline.gist: Comfort levels vary by culture and background, so spouses must reach clarity to avoid constant friction.

outline.heading: Her right to protection and the Prophet's vision
outline.gist: A wife can demand that he accompany or provide protection; the Prophet foresaw a woman travelling alone safely, so the mahram rule rests on necessity, not control.

outline.heading: Defaults and the right to revert
outline.gist: Either spouse may fall back to the default of provider and homemaker, with the other's financial or household share adjusting in turn.

outline.heading: Keep your own account
outline.gist: He encourages working wives to keep their money separate and pay for help from it, since pooled accounts breed confusion and resentment, as with a car bought from joint funds.

outline.heading: Household work equals earning
outline.gist: Islam treats maintaining the home as equal to providing, which makes each spouse grateful for the other's labour.

outline.heading: Clarity keeps marriage positive
outline.gist: Without clear roles everyone thinks they are doing more; the surah's rulings end at verse 7 and warnings follow.

outline.heading: Recap: oversight, timing and staying in the home
outline.gist: Divorce needs oversight, must happen in a state of purity without relations, and the wife stays home while he leaves.

outline.heading: Recap: reconciling, remarrying and the third divorce
outline.gist: Before the term ends they may reunite; afterwards a new contract is needed, and after a third divorce they must live separate lives.

outline.heading: Divorce is a decision, not a moment of anger
outline.gist: Witnesses are needed to leave just as to enter, since no one marries in a moment of passion.

outline.heading: The sheikh is the least important person at a nikah
outline.gist: A valid marriage needs only the groom, the bride's father, the bride and two witnesses; the officiant merely documents.

outline.heading: Recap: the waiting periods
outline.gist: Three months without cycles, and until the end of pregnancy for pregnant women however long that is.

outline.heading: Interlude
House them where you live, as far as you can
outline.gist: During the waiting period she stays in the marital home or one similar in space, safety and comfort to his own, within his means.

outline.heading: Do not harm them to squeeze them out
outline.gist: Men used their wealth to make wives' waiting periods miserable and pressure them to give up their rights; the verse forbids it.

outline.heading: Maintenance until a pregnant wife gives birth
outline.gist: If she is pregnant he supports her for the whole pregnancy, even beyond three months, which all four schools largely agree on.

outline.heading: Paying the mother for breastfeeding
outline.gist: Feeding the child is the father's duty, so if the mother nurses he compensates her; otherwise he pays for a wet nurse.

outline.heading: Agree with ma'ruf, or find another nurse
outline.gist: Set compensation by customary fairness; if they cannot agree, he arranges another way to feed the child.

outline.heading: The wealthy spend from their abundance
outline.gist: Maintenance is proportional to his wealth, not a fixed sum.

outline.heading: Qudira means restricted, not overpowered
outline.gist: The word for restricted provision also appears in the story of Yunus, who thought he would not be held to account, not that Allah could not reach him.

outline.heading: Ibn Abbas, Muawiyah and the story of Yunus
outline.gist: Ibn Abbas explained the word to a troubled Muawiyah; Yunus left his people in anger without permission, was swallowed by the whale, and his people later believed.

outline.heading: Allah burdens no one beyond what He gave
outline.gist: You cannot give what you were not given, a principle that sounds obvious but is rarely lived.

outline.heading: If you don't know, be quiet
outline.gist: Most arguments would vanish if people only spoke from what they were taught; find someone who knows.

outline.heading: Islam is to be learned, not debated
outline.gist: Like medicine or law, religion is discussed by the qualified; at family gatherings everyone is a doctor and a scholar except the actual ones.

outline.heading: Made-up statistics and imaginary Harvard studies
outline.gist: People invent precise numbers and studies to win points; truth never needs falsehood, and needing it shows a flawed understanding.

outline.heading: Play the hand you were dealt
outline.gist: You are asked only to do your best with what you were given; live within your means and stay humble.

outline.heading: Stop trying to impress
outline.gist: Being impressed is often a reflex of weakness that secretly hopes the other falls; the companions admired the Prophet in the healthy way.

outline.heading: After hardship, ease: provision comes in cycles
outline.gist: The promise is tied to provision: functional people do not stay poor forever, so give from what you have now.

outline.heading: Financial compatibility in marriage
outline.gist: A woman and her father may refuse a suitor who cannot keep her standard of living; the jurists even require a maid if she had one, unless she prefers simplicity.

outline.heading: The wife's own nafaqah
outline.gist: Beyond household costs, the wife is owed a personal allowance of roughly ten percent of his income, a right earlier poor generations never practised.

outline.heading: Why she leaves divorce with nothing
outline.gist: Deferred mahr is often token, so a homemaker ends up with nothing; Western fifty-fifty splits are better than zero but not the Islamic model.

outline.heading: Without nafaqah, marriage becomes leverage
outline.gist: A dependent wife without skills or savings can be mistreated; the allowance is agreed upon and owed unless income barely covers basics or she forgoes it.

outline.heading: Calculate unpaid nafaqah at divorce
outline.gist: If never paid, it should be computed year by year from his earnings and given to her, fairer than nothing or an even split.

outline.heading: The warnings ahead: these surahs are about women's rights
outline.gist: The coming verses warn because these rulings overturned the norms of the time; the theme could be called women's rights in Islam.

outline.heading: Outro

njQTWYqoiIk.title: Arabic Tafsir of Surat al-Qasas: Review of the Surah's Two Lessons
njQTWYqoiIk.one_line: A short review of al-Qasas: relationships shape our lives, we cannot judge people from their stories, and their motives are simple yet hidden.
njQTWYqoiIk.summary: In this short session the sheikh steps back to review the surah before continuing the commentary on Musa's story. Stories found in only one place in the Quran deserve slow reflection, and al-Qasas holds parts of Musa's story found nowhere else. He explains why he chose the group of surahs from al-Qasas to al-Sajdah: they deal with relationships, which more than anything make a person happy or miserable in this life. The Quran gives us the fruit of experience, as the wisdom of pre-Islamic poets did, so we need not waste years learning it ourselves. He restates the surah's two main points. First, we know others only as stories, so we can call an act right or wrong but cannot judge a person's life as a whole. Second, people's stories, however complicated, are driven by a few simple motives such as greed, desire, vanity and envy, yet we still cannot judge anyone's motive. He laments two centuries of Muslims suspecting one another to the point of declaring each other outside Islam, and urges making seventy excuses for a brother without giving up forbidding wrong. He illustrates with a man who raised his left finger in prayer because his right one was missing.

outline.gist: I can call a choice a sin or an obedience, but I cannot judge your life or choices as a whole from your story; only Allah knows.

outline.heading: Second lesson: simple motives, still hidden
outline.gist: Without learning and purification people are driven by greed, desire, vanity, envy and showing off, yet I may not judge anyone's motive; benefit, advise and show mercy instead.

28:49.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Then bring a scripture from the presence of Allah that giveth clearer guidance than these two (that) I may follow it, if ye are truthful

28:50.ar: فَإِن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لَكَ فَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّمَا يَتَّبِعُونَ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡۚ وَمَنۡ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ بِغَيۡرِ هُدࣰ ى مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
28:50.en: And if they answer thee not, then know that what they follow is their lusts. And who goeth farther astray than he who followeth his lust without guidance from Allah. Lo! Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

28:51.en: And now verily We have caused the Word to reach them, that haply they may give heed

28:52.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ هُم بِهِۦ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
28:52.en: Those unto whom We gave the Scripture before it, they believe in it

28:53.ar: وَإِذَا يُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡ قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ مُسۡلِمِينَ
28:53.en: And when it is recited unto them, they say: We believe in it. Lo! it is the Truth from our Lord. Lo! even before it we were of those who surrender (unto Him)

28:54.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُؤۡتَوۡنَ أَجۡرَهُم مَّرَّتَيۡنِ بِمَا صَبَرُواْ وَيَدۡرَءُونَ بِٱلۡحَسَنَةِ ٱلسَّيِّئَةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
28:54.en: These will be given their reward twice over, because they are steadfast and repel evil with good, and spend of that wherewith We have provided them

28:55.ar: وَإِذَا سَمِعُواْ ٱللَّغۡوَ أَعۡرَضُواْ عَنۡهُ وَقَالُواْ لَنَآ أَعۡمَٰلُنَا وَلَكُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلُكُمۡ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡ لَا نَبۡتَغِي ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ

QIAX7O5JtUI.title: Arabic Tafsir of Surat al-Qasas: The Quran's Challenge to the Masters of Arabic, Verses 49-53
QIAX7O5JtUI.one_line: Why the Quran's challenge struck at the Arabs' one mastery, following desire as the worst misguidance, and dawah as reminding people of what they know.
QIAX7O5JtUI.summary: The sheikh explains why the Quran, not Musa-style signs, was the Prophet's miracle. A miracle is something a prophet repeats as a challenge, and the Quran challenged the Arabs in the only art they had mastered. He spends a long stretch on that mastery: Arabic poetry's strict metre and rhyme, Arabic as an original root-based language that can derive new words where English absorbs any coinage, the link between vocabulary and intelligence, and the near-royal power of poets, told through al-A'sha's verse that lifted a poor man to honour and Ka'b ibn Zuhayr's coded ode answered by the Prophet's cloak. The Quran outdid them through recitation rules, sound and layered meaning, which he shows in the oath verses of al-'Adiyat, where a fed horse will die for its master while man is ungrateful to his Lord. 'Then know that they follow their desires' was told to the Prophet alone, so the surah's ban on judging stands; the lesson for us is never to follow desire without guidance. Verse 51's 'that they may remember', used three times in the surah, means people already hold the truth inside, so dawah should be reminding, not lecturing. Verses 52-53 praise earlier People of the Book who recognised the truth.

outline.heading: Miracle versus proofs of prophethood
outline.gist: A miracle must be repeated as a challenge; the splitting moon, water from his fingers and the weeping palm trunk are proofs of prophethood that strengthened the companions' faith.

outline.heading: The Quran's repeated challenges to the masters of speech
outline.gist: Bring a book, a discourse, ten surahs, one surah: the Arabs had orators like Aktham ibn Sayfi and Quss ibn Sa'idah.

outline.heading: The rigour of Arabic poetry and the Arabs' reverence for their language
outline.gist: English verse follows loose rhythm, while Arabic poetry is bound by strict metre and rhyme, yet the Arabs composed freely and prized their tongue before Islam.

outline.heading: The Prophet's challenge is the Book itself
outline.gist: Having heard of Musa's signs, the Prophet is told his proof is the book in his hands; those who cannot match it follow their desires.

outline.heading: Original and composite languages
outline.gist: Composite languages like English are flexible but lack roots; original ones are often rigid.

outline.heading: Arabic derives meaning from roots
outline.gist: Like mathematics, three letters yield 'alim, mu'allim and 'ilm; Arabic derives a new word when a new meaning appears, while English accepts arbitrary coinages.

outline.heading: Vocabulary and intelligence
outline.gist: A person's and a society's intelligence tracks their power to describe things in words, which prepared the Arabs to receive revelation.

outline.heading: Poets were honoured and feared like kings
outline.gist: Study pre-Islamic literature to see how much weight a poet's word carried.

outline.heading: Al-A'sha and al-Muhallaq
outline.gist: Pushed by his wife, a poor, idle Bedouin with nine unmarried daughters fed the great poet; one line of praise married off all nine and made him chief of his tribe.

outline.heading: The weight of the spoken word in Islam
outline.gist: Marriage, divorce and entering Islam all happen by a word; a spoken word becomes official and recorded.

outline.heading: The Quran overwhelmed the poets
outline.gist: Labid and Ka'b listened for more; al-A'sha set out to meet the Prophet but was talked out of it.

outline.heading: A challenge must be in the field you master
outline.gist: Challenging him at basketball would mean nothing; the Quran challenged the Arabs in eloquence, with its own art of recitation and a rhythm unlike poetry.

outline.heading: Depth beneath the surface
outline.gist: Much poetry is beautiful but empty, while the Quran carries firm creed, history and ethics, with a surface meaning and embedded messages the Arabs perceived.

outline.heading: Ka'b ibn Zuhayr comes to the Prophet
outline.gist: Son of the poet whose ode scholars memorised, Ka'b came disguised after his blood was declared lawful; his ode has only a couple of lines of praise and many about Su'ad and his camel.

outline.heading: Weeping over ruins as code
outline.gist: Ka'b was mourning his lost standing; poor teachers made students hate such poetry by missing its symbolism.

outline.heading: The Prophet's cloak restores his honour
outline.gist: Understanding the message, the Prophet laid his cloak on Ka'b, an honour his family inherited.

outline.heading: Layered meaning, not esoteric fantasy
outline.gist: This is a matter of language, not the batini sects; Musaylimah's imitation copied the rhythm with no meaning beneath.

outline.heading: Oath verses that describe and embed purpose
outline.gist: Al-Nazi'at and al-Dhariyat describe winds, clouds and angels while hinting at each creature's role in existence.

outline.heading: Al-'Adiyat: the loyal horse and the ungrateful human
outline.gist: The charging horse, its sparks and dust, will die for whoever feeds it, yet man is ungrateful to the Lord who created and provides for him.

outline.heading: 'Then know': told to the Prophet alone
outline.gist: The singular address means only the Prophet is told the inner state of those who reject; otherwise the surah's lesson against judging would be undone.

outline.heading: So the Prophet would not blame himself
outline.gist: He embodied the Quran, as Aisha said; when people reject us, the fault may be our poor example.

outline.heading: None more astray than one who follows desire without guidance
outline.gist: Desire and guidance usually pull in opposite directions; Dawud was warned not to follow desire, and no one should claim his desire has become aligned with the revelation.

outline.heading: The lesson: never be like them
outline.gist: The information is for our own warning, not to curse or gloat over the misguided.

outline.heading: Recitation: those who believed from among the People of the Book
outline.gist: He recites the five connected verses to be explained.

outline.heading: Revealed in parts, yet one connected whole
outline.gist: The Quran came over 23 years, verses placed as they came, yet it reads as a single continuous text, another side of its inimitability.

outline.heading: 'That they may remember', three times in the surah
outline.gist: The Quran's word choice is deliberate; al-Qasas repeats the same phrase in three verses.

outline.heading: People already know the truth; dawah is reminding
outline.gist: Good lies within the person far from Allah; no one has reminded him yet, so assume the best and aim to remind.

outline.heading: Reminding is finer than teaching
outline.gist: 'Remind, for reminding benefits' precedes the purpose of creation; the covenant of Alast placed la ilaha illa Allah inside every person.

outline.heading: Every word exactly right
outline.gist: The Arabs critiqued word choices in poetry but found none to improve in the Quran, and learned from its choices.

outline.heading: Who were given the Book before it?
outline.gist: After years of uncertainty he takes them to be earlier People of the Book, which fits the surah's axis best.

outline.heading: Our ummah is not the only one with good
outline.gist: Pray to be the best nation, but do not declare it in this world.

outline.heading: 'We were Muslims before it'
outline.gist: They had always submitted inwardly and recognised the truth at once.

28:56.ar: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهۡدِي مَنۡ أَحۡبَبۡتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
28:56.en: Lo! thou (O Muhammad) guidest not whom thou lovest, but Allah guideth whom He will. And He is Best Aware of those who walk aright

28:57.ar: وَقَالُوٓاْ إِن نَّتَّبِعِ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ مَعَكَ نُتَخَطَّفۡ مِنۡ أَرۡضِنَآۚ أَوَلَمۡ نُمَكِّن لَّهُمۡ حَرَمًا ءَامِنࣰ ا يُجۡبَىٰٓ إِلَيۡهِ ثَمَرَٰتُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ رِّزۡقࣰ ا مِّن لَّدُنَّا وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
28:57.en: And they say: If we were to follow the Guidance with thee we should be torn out of our land. Have We not established for them a sure sanctuary, whereunto the produce of all things is brought (in trade), a provision from Our presence? But most of them know not

28:58.ar: وَكَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا مِن قَرۡيَةِۭ بَطِرَتۡ مَعِيشَتَهَاۖ فَتِلۡكَ مَسَٰكِنُهُمۡ لَمۡ تُسۡكَن مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ اۖ وَكُنَّا نَحۡنُ ٱلۡوَٰرِثِينَ
28:58.en: And how many a community have We destroyed that was thankless for its means of livelihood! And yonder are their dwellings, which have not been inhabited after them save a little. And We, even We, were the inheritors

11:42.ar: وَهِيَ تَجۡرِي بِهِمۡ فِي مَوۡجࣲ كَٱلۡجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبۡنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِي مَعۡزِلࣲ يَٰبُنَيَّ ٱرۡكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
11:42.en: And it sailed with them amid waves like mountains, and Noah cried unto his son - and he was standing aloof - O my son! Come ride with us, and be not with the disbelievers

11:43.ar: قَالَ سَـَٔاوِيٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلࣲ يَعۡصِمُنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِۚ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَۚ وَحَالَ بَيۡنَهُمَا ٱلۡمَوۡجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُغۡرَقِينَ
11:43.en: He said: I shall betake me to some mountain that will save me from the water. (Noah) said: This day there is none that saveth from the commandment of Allah save him on whom He hath had mercy. And the wave came in between them, so he was among the drowned

6:74.ar: ۞وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ ءَازَرَ أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصۡنَامًا ءَالِهَةً إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰكَ وَقَوۡمَكَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
6:74.en: (Remember) when Abraham said unto his father Azar: Takest thou idols for gods? Lo! I see thee and thy folk in error manifest

5:18.ar: وَقَالَتِ ٱلۡيَهُودُ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ نَحۡنُ أَبۡنَٰٓؤُاْ ٱللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّٰٓؤُهُۥۚ قُلۡ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُم بِذُنُوبِكُمۖ بَلۡ أَنتُم بَشَرࣱ مِّمَّنۡ خَلَقَۚ يَغۡفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَلِلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَاۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
5:18.en: The Jews and Christians say: We are sons of Allah and His loved ones. Say: Why then doth He chastise you for your sins? Nay, ye are but mortals of His creating. He forgiveth whom He will, and chastiseth whom He will. Allah's is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and unto Him is the journeying

4:123.ar: لَّيۡسَ بِأَمَانِيِّكُمۡ وَلَآ أَمَانِيِّ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِۗ مَن يَعۡمَلۡ سُوٓءࣰ ا يُجۡزَ بِهِۦ وَلَا يَجِدۡ لَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيࣰّ ا وَلَا نَصِيرࣰ ا
4:123.en: It will not be in accordance with your desires, nor the desires of the People of the Scripture. He who doeth wrong will have the recompense thereof, and will not find against Allah any protecting friend or helper

4:124.ar: وَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ مِن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يَدۡخُلُونَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَا يُظۡلَمُونَ نَقِيرࣰ ا
4:124.en: And whoso doeth good works, whether of male or female, and he (or she) is a believer, such will enter paradise and they will not be wronged the dint in a date-stone

4:125.ar: وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ دِينࣰ ا مِّمَّنۡ أَسۡلَمَ وَجۡهَهُۥ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحۡسِنࣱ وَٱتَّبَعَ مِلَّةَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفࣰ اۗ وَٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ خَلِيلࣰ ا
4:125.en: Who is better in religion than he who surrendereth his purpose to Allah while doing good (to men) and followeth the tradition of Abraham, the upright? Allah (Himself) chose Abraham for friend

2:127.ar: وَإِذۡ يَرۡفَعُ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ ٱلۡقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلۡ مِنَّآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
2:127.en: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, (Abraham prayed): Our Lord! Accept from us (this duty). Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Hearer, the Knower
